Name: adaptive_online_compressive_SR_live
Title: Online Adaptive Compressive Super-Resolution Microscopy with Spatially-Temporally Consistent Diffusion Priors for Long-Term Live-Cell Nanoscopy
Experiment: We will validate the method on live HeLa cells expressing Lifeact-mNeonGreen (actin) and Rab5-mScarlet (endosomes) imaged at 37°C with a resonant-scanning confocal microscope modified for programmable compressive illumination using a digital micromirror device (DMD). Datasets will include: (1) static nanoparticle phantoms for calibration, (2) live-cell actin dynamics with varying undersampling ratios (4×, 8×, 12×, 16×), (3) endosome trafficking under pharmacological perturbations (Nocodazole, Brefeldin A). Baselines: (a) full STED acquisition (gold standard), (b) compressive sensing with fixed diffusion prior from static training, (c) compressive sensing with non-adaptive online prior (fixed update frequency), (d) total variation regularization. Metrics: spatial resolution by Fourier ring correlation (FRC) between reconstructions and full STED, temporal resolution (effective frame rate), PSNR/SSIM, single-particle tracking measures (localization precision, track length, diffusion coefficient extraction), photobleaching rate (fluorescence decay over time), and artifact quantification via residual error map analysis. Expected outcomes: Our adaptive method should achieve 50–60 nm resolution at 30+ frames per second sustained over thousands of frames, significantly reducing photobleaching compared to full STED, and maintaining high tracking fidelity (localization precision <10 nm) for dynamic structures. Ablation studies: (i) fixed vs. adaptive update rate of diffusion prior, (ii) with and without spatiotemporal consistency constraint, (iii) uniform vs. dynamic undersampling mask generation, (iv) sensitivity to initialization and prior batch size. We will also test generalization on additional cell types (U2OS, primary neurons) without retraining.
